items.stem: Private instances with no external IP need to download OS updates from the internet. What provides outbound access?

options.rationale: Correct: Cloud NAT gives private instances outbound internet access without external IPs.

options.text: Assigning each instance an external IP
options.rationale: That works but exposes instances and is not least-privilege.
Peering connects VPCs, not the public internet.
Internal load balancers route internal traffic, not internet egress.

items.explanation: Correct: Cloud NAT enables outbound internet access for instances without external IPs.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO are true about VPC firewall rules on Google Cloud? (Select TWO.)

options.text: They are stateful, so return traffic is allowed automatically
options.rationale: Correct: stateful rules permit return traffic without a reverse rule.

options.text: They can be scoped to instances using network tags
options.rationale: Correct: tags target rules to specific instances.

options.text: They require opening both directions for a single connection
options.rationale: Stateful rules do not need a separate return-direction rule.

options.text: They apply only to the default network
options.rationale: Rules apply to the VPC in which they are defined.

items.explanation: Correct: VPC firewall rules are stateful and can be scoped with network tags.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Two VPCs, A and B, are peered; B is peered with C. Can A reach C through B?

options.text: No, because VPC peering is non-transitive
options.rationale: Correct: peering does not provide transitive routing between A and C.

options.text: Yes, if A and C share a subnet
options.rationale: Shared subnets are not how peered VPCs route.

options.text: Only if Cloud NAT is enabled
options.rationale: NAT concerns internet egress, not inter-VPC routing.

items.explanation: Correct: VPC peering is non-transitive, so A cannot reach C through B.
